title: CLO 2025.1 - CLOFAB
description: CLO 2025.1 new version fully upgraded to further enhance your work efficiency! With the upgraded CLOFAB feature, you can quickly and accurately complete fabric digitization. This tool is specifically designed to be compatible with the new fabric digitization hardware CLO zFab Fabric Measurement Kit, ensuring seamless integration.
transcript:
This video is to introduce CloFab to you.  
The CloFab function makes it easy for you to create high-quality digital fabrics and immediately apply them to 3D clothing to check the effect.  
Before that, you must use a seamless fabric generator to create a pattern and a fabric generator to create physical properties.  
Starting from version 2025.1, you can use these two functions seamlessly in CloFab.  
In addition, by using the CloZFab fabric measurement kit, which is a new solution based on Clo’s latest AI technology, you can digitize fabric more accurately and faster.  
The CloZFab fabric measurement kit is a product for face-to-face corporate customer sales.  
We will provide a detailed user manual upon its release.  
Please stay tuned.  

Now, let’s see how to use it.  

There are three ways to open CloFab:  
First, if you want to start creating new fabrics from scratch, you can click the CloFab icon at the top of the window on the fabric selection card to activate the CloFab window and create new fabrics.  
Second, if you want to modify existing fabrics, you can click the icon on the right side of the fabric project in the object window, then select the physical property or the physical property option to start it from the list that appears.  
Finally, you can also start it from the main menu at the top by clicking on the Fabric menu, then clicking the CloFab submenu to start creating new fabrics.  

To check the results directly on 3D clothing, use Ctrl + A to select all versions and apply the newly added fabrics.  
The new fabric will be the default fabric.  
You can simulate the synchronization first.  

At the top of the window, enter the name of the fabric.  
If necessary, you can also enter the supplier and all related information.  

At the top is the preview area, which currently provides user manuals and related information about the ZFabKit.  
In the middle, the interface is mainly divided into the Physical Property and Physical Property Selection cards.  
The basic workflow is to create a physical property first, then start the project and set the physical property.  
But if you already have a sticker, you can directly enter the Physical Property Selection card and generate only the physical property.  
You can also see relevant introductions and links at the top.  

Let’s start with the Physical Property Selection card.  
At the bottom of this card, you can choose how to create a physical sticker.  
If you have a CloZFab scanning device, you can use the first option.  
Opening an image is based on the image file you already have to create a fabric sticker.  
Even if you don’t have a scanning device, you can still use this option.  

I will click it to import the file.  
At this point, if you follow the specified file naming rules, you can automatically add a PBR sticker to the same file.  

When opening the image, it will first display the crop frame, which is convenient for you to cut out unnecessary areas on the fabric.  
You can drag the screen to center the crop frame.  
Use the four corners or the handles on the sides to adjust the crop area.  
To move the position of the crop area, just click and drag.  
If you want to redo the crop, please click the redo button in the upper right corner.  

After adjusting the crop area to keep the required part of the fabric, click the selection icon in the upper right corner or press the return key on the keyboard to complete the crop.  

After cropping is completed, you will enter the seamless processing step.  
You need to find the repeat area in the fabric texture.  
Select the automatic option in the selection screen menu and then select the pattern type of the fabric.  
The system will display this in the top right corner of the screen.  
It will automatically analyze the best effect in the designated area.  

You can choose between two pattern types:  
- The repeat type is used for evenly repeating patterns, for example, grid patterns.  
- The single-color irregular type is used for fabrics with no specific pattern or irregularly distributed patterns.  

Please note that this type is based on the information from the line drawing, so there must be a line drawing to get the correct result.  

For this fabric, I will choose the repeat type and drag to define the repeat area.  
The automatic analysis part will be displayed as a grid.  
You can preview the repeat results based on the selected area.  
When selecting an area with four pattern repetitions, the automatic evaluation effect is the most accurate and efficient.  

You can view the seamless effect at the top.  
Open the grid display to check the repeat unit.  
Click the switch menu icon on the left side to check the status of each image.  
You can also select repeat area calculation again at the bottom.  

If the brightness of the result is uneven, you can use the average function in the adjustment panel.  
Enter a number or adjust the slider to correct it.  

Next, let’s see how to manually set the repeat area.  
To switch to manual mode, you can directly uncheck the automatic option in the settings panel or click the button in the lower right corner of the selected area to switch modes.  

After entering manual mode, you can directly adjust the selected area.  
You can adjust the corners and edges using the handles to modify the selected area.  
Of course, you can also refresh the selection and then adjust again.  

Now I will align the four points of the selected area to the same position.  
After you are satisfied with the selection, click the checkmark button to confirm.  
The upper preview window will show the result of the manually selected area.  
Click Apply.  
You can check the texture effect on the 3D clothing.  

Next, click on the Physical Property option card to create a physical property.  
At the top, there is a button for the CloZFab fabric test device.  
It is a toggle menu.  
If you have a CloZFab fabric test device, you can use it anytime.  
Even if you don’t have one, you can easily create the correct fabric properties for your clothing.  

All you need to do is enter the material and weight of the fabric type.  
First, select the fabric type.  
The component items that can be used will change according to the fabric type, so please click in order to choose.  

Next, enter the component information.  
First, select the fiber type and enter the content percentage of each component.  
Then enter the weight and thickness of the fabric.  

In the preview at the top, you can see the actual 3D drape effect based on the information you entered.  
The texture sticker we created earlier will also be reflected in this preview.  
There will also be three preset texture pictures of the fabric type below.  
Click to switch between them.  
Click again to switch back to the original texture.  

Click Apply below.  
The physical property can then be applied to 3D clothing.  
Open the simulation to check the effect on the body.  

Through the model type drop-down menu in the upper left corner of the window, you can check the fabric’s versatility under different conditions.  
You can control the visual image in the preview window just like in the 3D window.  
You can lock the custom visual image by clicking the lock icon.  

Click the arrow next to the detailed information to directly edit the generated physical properties.  
But please remember that manually changing these values means you will alter the results based on the original fabric information input.  
In other words, the physical properties will no longer correspond to the input data.  
Therefore, be very careful when making adjustments.  

After fabric creation is complete, you can use the buttons at the bottom to apply or save your work.  
If you want to save the fabric as a ZFAB file, please click the save button in the lower left corner.  

In the preview image menu, you can choose which type of image to use as the fabric preview in the library.  
By default, the fabric sticker image is applied, but you can also add a custom image according to your needs.  

Through the save function, you can choose which stickers and fabric files to save together.  
You can choose to save only the usable PBR sticker.  
Select the stickers to be saved.  

After saving the sticker, click Confirm. The file resource manager window will appear.  
The fabric will be saved with the name you defined in CloFab.  
If it contains stickers, it will automatically generate other file names for each type of sticker.  

Finally, if you click the New button, the content in each option card will be reset to the initial state.  

Now let’s take a look through the library at previously saved fabrics and their PBR stickers.  

I hope you can use the new CloFab to create more efficient and high-quality digital fabrics.  
Thank you for watching.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.1 - CLOFAB
chunks.content: # CLO 2025.1 - CloFab: Digital Fabric Creation and Application This document explains the functionality, workflow, and technical details of CloFab in CLO version 2025.1, a tool designed for creating high-quality digital fabrics with physical properties and applying them to 3D clothing. It also covers integration with the CloZFab fabric measurement kit, fabric pattern processing, and fabric property creation. --- ## Introduction to CloFab and CloZFab Integration This section introduces CloFab, a function in CLO 2025.1 for seamless creation and application of digital fabrics, and the CloZFab fabric measurement kit, a new AI-based solution for accurate and efficient fabric digitization. - **CloFab** combines a seamless fabric generator (for pattern creation) and a fabric generator (for physical properties) into one unified tool. - **CloZFab Fabric Measurement Kit** is a new hardware solution leveraging AI technology to digitize fabric properties faster and more accurately. - CloZFab is available for face-to-face corporate sales with a detailed user manual forthcoming. --- ## Accessing CloFab There are three methods to open and start using CloFab: 1. **Creating New Fabrics from Scratch** - Click the CloFab icon on the fabric selection card at the top of the window. 2. **Modifying Existing Fabrics** - Click the icon beside the fabric project in the object window and select the physical property option from the list. 3. **Using the Main Menu** - Navigate to the Fabric menu, then select the CloFab submenu to create new fabrics. To apply new fabrics to 3D clothing, use **Ctrl + A** to select all versions and apply the fabrics, which will become the default. Simulation synchronization is available for preview. --- ## CloFab User Interface Overview The CloFab window is divided into three main areas: - **Top Area:** Fabric name input, supplier information, and preview pane displaying user manuals and CloZFab information. - **Middle Area:** Two main cards—Physical Property Selection and Physical Property creation. - **Bottom Area:** Controls for importing fabric images and creating physical properties. The typical workflow: 1. Create or select a **physical property**. 2. Start or modify the fabric project using that property. If a fabric sticker (texture) exists, you can directly use the Physical Property Selection card to generate physical properties. --- ## Creating Fabric Stickers and Seamless Patterns This section covers fabric sticker creation from images, including cropping, seamless pattern processing, and repeat area definition. ### Importing and Cropping Fabric Images - Import image files following specified naming rules to auto-assign PBR (Physically Based Rendering) stickers. - Crop the fabric image to exclude unnecessary areas using draggable corners and edges. - Use the redo button to reset cropping. - Confirm cropping by clicking the selection icon or pressing the return key. ### Seamless Pattern Processing - After cropping, proceed to define the **repeat area** of the fabric. - Two pattern types are supported: - **Repeat Type:** For evenly repeating patterns like grids. - **Single-Color Irregular Type:** For fabrics without a clear pattern or with irregular patterns (requires a line drawing).

chunks.content: - Crop the fabric image to exclude unnecessary areas using draggable corners and edges. - Use the redo button to reset cropping. - Confirm cropping by clicking the selection icon or pressing the return key. ### Seamless Pattern Processing - After cropping, proceed to define the **repeat area** of the fabric. - Two pattern types are supported: - **Repeat Type:** For evenly repeating patterns like grids. - **Single-Color Irregular Type:** For fabrics without a clear pattern or with irregular patterns (requires a line drawing). - Use the **automatic option** to let the system analyze and select the best repeat area. - Preview the seamless repeat effect; a grid display helps visualize the repeat unit. - Automatic evaluation is most accurate with an area containing four pattern repetitions. - If brightness is uneven, use the average function with a slider or numeric input to adjust. ### Manual Repeat Area Adjustment - Switch off automatic mode to manually define the repeat area. - Adjust the selection corners and edges using handles. - Refresh selection as needed. - Align points precisely for accurate repeat definition. - Confirm with the checkmark button. - Preview updates automatically. - Apply the repeat pattern to see the effect on 3D clothing. --- ## Creating Physical Fabric Properties This section explains how to define physical attributes of fabrics using CloFab or the CloZFab device. ### Using CloZFab Fabric Test Device - Toggle the CloZFab device option if you have the hardware. - The device facilitates direct measurement and input of fabric properties. ### Manual Physical Property Input - Select fabric type from a dropdown; available component items update accordingly. - Enter component fiber types and their percentage contents. - Input fabric weight and thickness. - The preview displays 3D draping effects based on input data and applied fabric sticker. - Three preset texture images per fabric type are available for preview toggling. - Apply physical properties to 3D clothing and open simulation to verify effects. ### Additional Controls and Warnings - Use the **model type dropdown** to test fabric behavior across different conditions. - Visual image controls in the preview mimic 3D window controls; lock images as needed. - Editing detailed physical property values manually is possible but will disconnect the properties from the original input data—use caution to avoid inaccurate results. --- ## Saving and Managing Fabric Files This section details saving fabric projects, fabric stickers, and preview images. - Use **Save** button to store fabric as a ZFAB file. - Customize which stickers and fabric files to save, including only usable PBR stickers. - After saving, a file resource manager appears showing saved files with names based on the CloFab fabric name and sticker types. - Preview image selection in the fabric library defaults to the fabric sticker but can be customized. - Use the **New** button to reset all input fields and start fresh. --- ## Browsing and Reusing Saved Fabrics - Access previously saved fabrics and their PBR stickers through the library interface.

The CloZFab measurement kit enhances this with AI-driven digitization for greater accuracy. The tool supports image import, cropping, pattern repeat definition (automatic/manual), and detailed physical property input, with real-time 3D previews and simulation. Careful management of saved fabric files and stickers ensures efficient reuse and project organization.
